column1: # The last row is the terminal `*` row: it asserts the walk is COMPLETE.
# frontier.py refuses a plan without it and re-checks the final state in its
# exit code, so a truncated plan fails instead of reporting a shorter frontier.
# WHAT THIS PLAN MEASURES.  On the pre-merge frontend a method has no
# per-declaration quarantine (raft-w2 handoff H-3), so EVERY unlowerable
# method refuses the whole export and must be neutralised for the walk to
# continue.  Reaching a clean export therefore takes 36 body replacements + 9
# rewrites + 1 injected probe file, plus 25 import-drop rows that are pure
# artefacts of the walk itself (a replaced body orphans its file's imports).
# The POST-MERGE plan (frontier-plan-postmerge.tsv) needs 14 rows over the
# same tree, and only 3 of those stand for gaps a per-declaration quarantine
# cannot catch.  The difference between the two plans is the measurement.
# READ THE EXPECTATIONS AS "WHAT THE FRONTEND SAID AT THAT STEP", not as the
# cause of that declaration's refusal.  The frontend reports ONE refusal at a
# time and does not name the declaration carrying it, so a row's expectation
# is the message observed when that row ran — for a declaration with several
# unlowerable constructs it may name a different one than the census
# attributes.  The per-declaration causes are the QUARANTINE CENSUS in
# docs/raft-w3-log.md §2, taken from the post-merge wire where every
# Rows whose declaration column starts with `$` are PROBE DELTAS standing in
# for recorded gaps (docs/raft-w3-log.md §3): they touch the walk's work copy
# ORDER: generated by walking, then re-verified by frontier.py against this
# file (the tracked instrument's own check).  Regenerate after any subject or
# frontend change; do not hand-edit rows.
